(all four at H2, the same level as their own grandparent `## D.31 Date and time handling` at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:48152 and as `## Annex D` at :41493, while the sibling clause `### D.31.5.1 General` at :48329 is at H3)
claim.why_it_matters: The Annex D clause hierarchy is flattened: D.31.5.8-.11 render as peers of Annex D and of D.32 instead of children of D.31.5. TOC/outline navigation and any heading-level-driven section extraction mis-nest these clauses, and the inconsistency with D.31.5.1 (H3) proves it is a transcription artifact, not a deliberate scheme. No normative text is lost - navigational only. It is a document-wide pattern in Annex D (D.31.2.6-.7, D.31.3.3-.9, D.31.5.2-.7 are flattened the same way), so repair should be an Annex D sweep, not a one-page edit.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Nothing on page 1199 is missing, and the PDF contains no heading-level information for the markdown to have lost. 1. NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind is labelled 'missing-heading', but all four headings are present in the markdown verbatim, in order, with their full clause numbers and titles (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:48420 D.31.5.8, :48425 D.31.5.9, :48430 D.31.5.10, :48435 D.31.5.11), each with its complete body paragraph and its own `` anchor. I diffed the rendered page against page-1199.md: every sentence of the four clauses, the run-on paragraph from D.31.5.7 at the top, and the D.32 heading are all transcribed correctly. There is zero text loss. 2. THE PDF ENCODES NO HEADING LEVEL, SO NONE CAN BE 'LOST'. This is the load-bearing point, and I checked the printed glyphs myself rather than assuming. In ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex D every clause heading, at every depth, is set in ONE uniform bold face at ONE uniform size. On the rendered page 1199 the fourth-level 'D.31.5.8 INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function' and the second-level 'D.32 Alternatives to HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC...' are typographically indistinguishable. Measuring the glyph band heights at 300 dpi: D.31.5.8 = 34px, D.31.5.9 = 32px, D.32 (2nd level) = 35px; and on page 1196, D.31.4 (3rd level) = 34px, D.31.4.1 (4th level) = 34px, D.31.5.1 (4th level) = 34px. Identical face, identical size, identical indent across the 2nd, 3rd and 4th levels. The PDF carries the hierarchy EXCLUSIVELY in the dotted decimal number — and the markdown preserves that number intact in every heading's text. So there is no attribute in the source that the transcription failed to reproduce. The `##`-vs-`###` depth is a markdown markup convention invented by the transcriber; it has no counterpart in the canonical document. A PDF-vs-markdown reconciliation cannot find a discrepancy in a property the PDF does not express. 3. THE CLAIM'S OWN 'PROOF' IS INTERNALLY BROKEN. The claim argues the inconsistency with `### D.31.5.1` proves an artifact. But D.31.5.1's H3 is not the correct baseline either: its parent `## D.31.5 International date and time format handling` is itself at H2 (:48326), the same level as `## D.31` (:48152). So under the claim's preferred scheme D.31.5 still renders as a SIBLING of D.31 rather than its child, and D.31.5.1 at H3 is still mis-nested. Neither branch of the cited inconsistency matches the clause numbering, which means the H3 cases are not a 'correct scheme' that the H2 cases departed from — the whole transcription simply uses H2 as its general-purpose heading level (`## Annex D` at :41493 and `## Concepts` at :41496 sit at H2 too, with H1 reserved for the per-page running header `# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)`). That is a global convention, not a page-1199 defect. 4. NO MEANING CHANGES, AND NOTHING NAVIGATIONAL IS ACTUALLY LOST. The claim concedes no normative text is affected. Even the asserted navigational harm does not hold: any TOC builder or section extractor can recover the exact depth of 'D.31.5.8' by counting the dots in the clause number that is right there in the heading text — the same and only mechanism the printed standard itself offers a human reader. This falls squarely in the reject categories: the allegedly missing text is present, and the residual difference is markup formatting that does not change meaning. If the transcription's heading depths are to be regularized for tooling convenience, that is a self-consistency cleanup of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, not a fidelity defect against the PDF, and it should not be carried in the spec-reconciliation ledger as a PDF discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. All four clause headings (D.31.5.8, D.31.5.9, D.31.5.10, D.31.5.11) and all of their body text are transcribed on page 1199 completely and verbatim; nothing is missing despite the 'missing-heading' label. The only difference alleged is markdown heading depth, and the PDF does not encode heading depth at all: ISO Annex D prints 2nd-, 3rd- and 4th-level clause headings in a single uniform bold face at a single uniform size (measured 32-35px glyph height for D.32, D.31.4, D.31.4.1, D.31.5.1, D.31.5.8 and D.31.5.9 alike), carrying hierarchy solely through the dotted decimal number, which the markdown preserves intact. The cited contrast with `### D.31.5.1` is an internal inconsistency of the transcription rather than evidence of infidelity, and its 'correct' branch is itself mis-nested because the parent `## D.31.5` also sits at H2. At most this is an optional self-consistency cleanup of the markdown's own heading-level convention across Annex D; it is not a content or fidelity defect and does not belong in the reconciliation ledger.
